solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Anchor showing unusual stamina, say — finally

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of stamina appear in an unfamiliar order
finally points to the closing letter of the word say

explanation.surface: Someone praised as a steadfast anchor for their remarkable stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STAMINA to MAINSTA; 'finally' takes Y from 'say'. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a person or thing that holds everything steady is a chief support, like an anchor.

clue.text: Works, lacking time for paintings

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is dropped from the word for works

parts.note: works hard means toils

explanation.surface: An artist's output viewed as paintings minus a dating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' as a verb gives TOILS; 'lacking' drops T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are commonly just called oils, after the medium used.

clue.text: Went quickly, getting bitten

definitions.meaning: to nip out or nip off is a British colloquialism for going somewhere briefly and fast
a nip is a small bite, so this is being given one

explanation.surface: Someone dashing off after being nipped by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one past-tense verb: dashing briefly somewhere, and being given a small bite.

clue.text: Fires half of main agents protecting king

indicators.note: half of takes the second pair of letters of the word main
protecting says the spies surround the king, enclosing him

parts.note: secret agents are spies
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something fires up half the main agents who guard the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the back half of 'main'; 'protecting' wraps the agents round the king. 'Fires' reads as a noun but is a verb, as in fires up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stimulate or motivate them, the figurative sense here.

clue.text: Fish batter covering last of chips is rubbish

indicators.note: in a down answer, covering puts one piece on top of the next

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word chips

parts.note: to batter is to hit hard, to wallop

explanation.surface: Fish in batter around chips sounds tasty but is called nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the fish sits on top of the chips' last letter in this down light. The chip-shop surface hides 'batter' as a verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, a synonym of rubbish in the sense of foolish talk.

clue.text: Legendarily careless cook's adder flan partly sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A careless cook's flan made with a snake is returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend King Alfred, sheltering in a peasant's hut, let the cakes burn; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English king of Wessex is famously remembered in a folk tale for burning cakes he was minding.

clue.text: Make the most of saying one's right of course

parts.note: a maxim is a saying or proverb
one is gives I and S, the numeral one plus the contracted is

indicators.note: right of takes the rightmost letter of the word course

explanation.surface: Advice to exploit a proverb that is naturally correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right of' takes E, the rightmost letter of 'course'. 'of course' looks like a phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to increase it to the greatest possible extent, making full use of it.

clue.text: Guy perhaps having topless challenge eating fruit

indicators.note: eating says one piece takes in the other
topless removes the first letter, which in a down light is the top

parts.note: to defy is to challenge
a fig is a fruit

explanation.surface: A guy taking on a topless dare while munching fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves EFY; 'eating' takes in the fruit. A guy is the Guy Fawkes effigy burned on Bonfire Night, 5 November, in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy, burned on Bonfire Night, is an example of a crude likeness of a person made to be burned.

clue.text: Pasta nut

definitions.meaning: a ribbon or strand of dough boiled in water, such as Chinese egg pasta
nut is slang for the head, as is this word

explanation.surface: A dish of pasta with a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a strip of pasta and, colloquially, the head or brain.

clue.text: Responsibility — it's our treat!

definitions.meaning: a burden or duty that falls on someone
read as two words, the phrase someone says when paying for others

explanation.surface: Picking up the bill and shouldering the duty of paying.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived word means burden or duty, and split in two it is what a host says when paying.

clue.text: A crust for father's endeavour following promotion?

indicators.note: following says the father's piece comes after the promotion piece

parts.note: a puff is a piece of promotional praise
pa is father, with the possessive s
a try is an attempt or endeavour

explanation.surface: Asking whether a crust follows a father's career push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the father's attempt after the promotion; 'for' is a link. The question mark marks the whimsical father's-career reading.
explanation.definitionFit: This light, flaky pastry is a kind of crust used on pies and tarts.

clue.text: Some said I put savings back, being daft

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read in reverse order
some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly reversing a savings decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes DIPUTS from 'said I put savings'; 'back' turns it round. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is British for foolish or unintelligent, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Scheme and lie about rocket, for example

parts.note: a project is a scheme or plan

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of lie are moved around

explanation.surface: A rocket programme mired in plotting and lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIE to ILE. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one example of a missile, an object propelled through the air.

clue.text: Backing tabloid, captures awards

indicators.note: backing says the word for tabloid is turned round

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper
to land a fish or a deal is to capture it

explanation.surface: Supporting a tabloid that wins prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns RAG into GAR; the surface makes it sound like support.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreaths of flowers are given as honours, so these are prizes or accolades.

clue.text: The old old chap? A farmer in times gone by

definitions.text: A farmer in times gone by

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Asking whether an elderly fellow was a farmer of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a small freeholder who farmed his own land in England was called this.

clue.text: Spray from a cat is here inside

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

indicators.note: inside takes the inner letters of the word here

explanation.surface: A cat spraying inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' takes ER, the inner letters of 'here'. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: A year in ghetto's refuge

indicators.note: in says the year letter goes into the ghetto word

parts.note: a slum is a ghetto, with the possessive dropped

explanation.surface: A year spent in a ghetto's shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection given to someone fleeing danger, a place of safety.

clue.text: Young lady admits gate money errors

indicators.note: admits says the young lady takes the gate money inside

parts.note: miss is a title for a young lady
the take is money collected, such as entry receipts at a gate

explanation.surface: A young lady confessing to errors in the ticket takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' reads as a confession but means takes in. Gate money is the takings at a sports ground's entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakes and errors are synonyms for things done wrongly.

clue.text: Points of contention in numbers

definitions.meaning: editions of a magazine are numbers

explanation.surface: Disputes over figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Matters in dispute and successive editions of a periodical share one word.

clue.text: Programme chosen to include the Spanish steps

indicators.note: to include says one piece goes inside the other
programme as a verb means to set up or rearrange, so the letters of chosen are reordered

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A TV programme selected to feature the Spanish Steps in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programme' rearranges the letters to ECHONS; 'to include' takes in the Spanish article. The surface evokes Rome's Spanish Steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Echelons are levels or ranks in a hierarchy, like steps on a ladder.

clue.text: Feature on head of this zoo losing specs for material

indicators.note: in a down light, on places the feature above the next piece

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word this
losing removes letters from the word zoo

parts.note: specs, or spectacles, look like the two round letters

explanation.surface: A zoo animal's face shown wearing glasses, on fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing specs' drops OO, two letters shaped like a pair of glasses, from ZOO, leaving Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a printed glazed cotton fabric, often floral, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Meal of mushy peas in empty restaurant

indicators.note: in says the peas go inside the emptied restaurant
empty leaves only the outer letters of the word restaurant
mushy says the letters of peas are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A dish of mushy peas served in a deserted restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' rearranges PEAS to EPAS; 'empty' leaves RT. Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: Primate's right hand suppressing potential uses

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down light, suppressing places these letters on top of the next piece
potential says the letters of uses could form something else

explanation.surface: A primate's right hand holding down possible uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges to ESUS, which sits beneath right and hand in this down light, as 'suppressing' says.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, and monkeys are primates.

clue.text: Little girl gets second testimonial to give out

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a tribute is a testimonial

explanation.surface: A young girl receives a second reference to hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out or deal out to several people.

clue.text: Small container routed through west of Liverpool

parts.note: via means by way of, routed through

indicators.note: west of takes the leftmost, first letter of the word Liverpool

explanation.surface: A small container sent via the west side of Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Run checks on opening of Olympic bar

parts.note: to vet is to run checks on

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of the word Olympic

explanation.surface: Checking a bar at the opening of the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a ban, so to veto is to bar.

clue.text: Prime Minister rejecting fish after a case of treatment

indicators.note: after says the fish comes following the earlier letters
case of takes the outer letters of the word treatment
rejecting says the fish is turned back

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister refusing fish after treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives TT; 'rejecting' turns EEL to LEE. Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain as Prime Minister in the postwar Labour government.

clue.text: Illegal occupant, short and stocky, they're regularly chasing

indicators.note: chasing says the following letters come after the first piece

parts.note: squat means short and thickset

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of the word they're

explanation.surface: A short stocky intruder being pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: A squatter is someone occupying a building without legal right.
